description: Mann-Whitney U test: U1 = R1 - n1 (n1 + 1) / 2 from the average ranks of x in x and y, and its p-value; method 0 automatic (exact if n1 <= 8 or n2 <= 8 and no ties, else 2), 1 exact null distribution, 2 normal approximation with the tie correction and the continuity correction, 3 the same without the continuity correction; alternative -1 less, 0 two-sided (twice the tail at max(U1, U2), at most 1), 1 greater

tolerance.reason: For both outputs, by the rule of ttest_1samp. U1 is a sum of half-integer ranks, exact in double arithmetic, so its condition number in the data is 0 and only the few rounded operations in s move z, counted generously as n = n1 + n2; the exact p-value is a ratio of exact counts (kappa_p = 1), the asymptotic one adds kappa_p = |z phi(z) / Q| (mannwhitneyu_rounding_bound). The largest bound max(kappa_p, 1) n 2^-53 on this grid is 8.6e-14 (n1 = 10, n2 = 25, x above y, without continuity correction: z = 4.6); 1e-13 is the smallest round value above it (tested). SciPy's worst error is 2.1e-15

grid: x the first n1 and y the next n2 of v_i = (7919 i) mod 1000, x shifted by d: sizes (n1, n2) in {(3, 6), (6, 3), (4, 5), (5, 4), (8, 8), (8, 20), (20, 8)} with methods 0 to 3, and {(9, 9), (10, 25), (25, 10)} with methods 0, 2 and 3, for d in {-1000.5, -200.5, 0.5, 150.5, 1000.5} (all values distinct); tied samples with v_i rounded down to a multiple of 200, sizes {(4, 5), (8, 8), (10, 25)}, d in {-1000, -200, 0, 200, 1000}, methods 0, 2 and 3; each with alternative -1 (less), 0 (two-sided) and 1 (greater). U1 from 0 to 250 (54 points with a half-integer U1), p-value from 3.2e-7 to 1
